messages:
emma_h: Hey team, newbie question — I followed the README and started the compose stack, but my app (running on host) dials Postgres over a unix socket (DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///redwood?host=/var/run/postgresql) and gets "connect() to unix domain socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432" failed: No such file or directory". Redis is similar — our app expects a socket but compose creates the container-only socket. How do others handle this?

ryan_t: Welcome! Unix sockets are convenient but brittle across host/container. If your app runs on host it can't see a socket inside the Postgres container at /var/run/postgresql. Two options: 1) run the app inside compose so it shares the container network and can use service names, or 2) use TCP host:port (e.g., DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/redwood).

emma_h: We're doing host dev for fast reloads. Is it safe to bind the container socket to the host path (e.g., - ./pg_socket:/var/run/postgresql) so host app can use it?

benji: That can work but on mac it often fails because Docker Desktop mounts behave differently and socket ownership can block Postgres from creating the socket. Named volumes + port mapping is simpler: expose 5432 on localhost and use TCP. If you really want sockets, I'd recommend running the entire stack (web included) inside compose.

ops-bot: Note: The onboarding doc recommends service hostnames or remapped ports for host dev: https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services#host-vs-container

ryan_t: If you want to try a quick toggle: in .env.local set DATABASE_URL to `postgres://redwood:pass@localhost:54320/redwood_dev` and change compose to map `54320:5432` for the db. That avoids colliding with any local postgres you may have. Same for Redis: `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:63790` and map `63790:6379` in compose.

emma_h: Good tip. I guess remapping ports is safer than socket bind. But is there a way to keep socket for performance parity when inside Docker? I care about dev parity with CI which uses sockets sometimes.

benji: CI usually uses containerized services so sockets are internal. For host dev, parity is about behavior, not exact transport. We keep tests agnostic to TCP vs socket. If you care about performance, measure in CI or run an isolated container that simulates socket behavior.

ryan_t: If you want to experiment with host socket approach, you can mount a host directory for the socket and ensure perms: `volumes: - ./pgsocket:/var/run/postgresql` then `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgsocket` (replace 999 with postgres uid in image). But again, on mac this is flaky.

emma_h: I changed to remapped ports and updated .env.local, app connects over TCP now. One follow-up: when I switched REDIS_URL from socket to TCP I got `ECONNREFUSED` until I updated the app env — quick way to confirm compose picked up new port?

ryan_t: `docker-compose ps` will show the ports column. Also `docker-compose logs redis` and `docker ps --format "{{.Names}} {{.Ports}}" | grep redis` to verify mapping.

dev-env-bot: Tip: For host dev we have a sample `.env.local.example` in the repo with remapped ports. See https://redwood.example/docs/onboarding/local-services#env-local

emma_h: Awesome — thanks all. I'll stick to remapped TCP ports for now and try running the web container later to validate full parity. Appreciate the help! :raised_hands:
